newsitem.title: USA: Bolstering financial mkts key in Asia - US's Shafer.
newsitem.headline: Bolstering financial mkts key in Asia - US's Shafer.

text.p: Deepening and broadening financial markets in Asia is critical to further economic development of the region, a senior Clinton administration official said on Wednesday.

"It's clear that much stronger capital market flows are needed to finance infrastructure," Jeffrey Shafer, the U.S. Treasury's undersecretary for international affairs, told a symposium at Georgetown University Law Center.

"In Asia, the equity markets have been growing but there is a gap in the availability of long-term debt," said Shafer, who also said the Group of Seven nations has taken a strong interest in the strengthening of financial markets.
Long-term financing is crucial to building infrastructure, Shafer said, pointing to the need in Asia for the development of 20- to 30-year bond markets.
A step in that direction might be the further development of government bond markets to provide benchmarks for private capital markets, but Shafer said that would only be a first step.

He said breaking down legal and regulatory barriers to issuance of stocks and bonds was also important, as was support for institutional investment and reduction of barriers to international investment.

Additionally, Shafer stressed the need for sound market infrastructure, which he said included greater disclosure requirements and a regulatory structure that ensures the safety and soundness of the system.

Shafer, however, said he was optimistic on the outlook for Asia overall, saying, "The harder-to-figure-out parts of the growth puzzle have been solved. I'm convinced we can make progress on these issues."
